interpretation.outcome: A personal food log that keeps every meal you eat, with amounts and calories, so you can see daily totals, past days, and how you trend over time.
interpretation.main_input: Quick entries you type as you eat: the food, how much, and its calories.
interpretation.useful_result: Log a meal in seconds, see today's total against your target, scroll back through history, and see a weekly average trend.
important_assumptions: Entries are timestamped automatically, and the date and time can be changed.
Meals are grouped as breakfast, lunch, dinner and snack.
Amounts are a number plus a unit you type, such as 150 g or 1 bowl.
Days run midnight to midnight in your local time.
Everything stays on your Mac and is yours to edit or delete.

first.reply:
Got it — this is reusable, not a one-off, so Alpha will build it as an app: quick entry per meal, daily calorie totals, full history, and weekly trends.

One honest limit: record storage and the on-screen interface aren't connected yet, and neither is automatic calorie estimation from a food name. The brief captures the app as you want it, and Alpha builds it when those arrive.

Three quick things to get the shape right:

questions.question: Will you type the calories yourself, or should the app estimate them from the food name and amount?
options: Estimate, but let me correct it
questions.why_it_matters: Typing your own works with today's plan; automatic estimates need a capability that isn't connected yet and would always be shown as correctable guesses.

questions.question: Do you have a daily calorie target to track against?
questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether the daily view shows a plain total or a total against a goal with calories remaining.

questions.question: Besides calories, do you want to track anything else per food?
questions.why_it_matters: Knowing now keeps entry fast and makes the trends show the numbers you actually care about.

assumptions.text: Entries are timestamped automatically and can be back-dated.
Meals are grouped as breakfast, lunch, dinner, snack.
Amount is a number plus a free-text unit (150 g, 1 bowl, 2 slices).
A day is midnight to midnight, local time.
History is kept until you delete it; nothing leaves your Mac.
Trends default to daily totals plus a 7-day average.

first.reply:
I'll set this up as a one-off task: you paste your meeting notes, and Alpha returns a clean one-page brief — summary, decisions, action items with owner and due date, open questions.

Two limits, straight up: Alpha can't open a notes file you pick, and can't save the brief as a document yet, so you paste notes in and copy the brief out. It also reuses your own wording rather than rewriting it, since runtime rewriting isn't connected yet.

questions.question: Which sections must the brief always include?

No — leave blank if not in my notes

Notes arrive as plain pasted text, including bullets or rough shorthand.

Nothing is stored between runs.
Dates found in the notes are repeated exactly as written, not converted.

first.reply: Good news and a limit. This is recurring, so Alpha will keep it as a small daily solution: read today's Ahmedabad forecast, write a warm short message, send it to your mom on WhatsApp each morning. questions.why_it_matters: The message should land before she starts her day.

full_conversation.reply: Good news and a limit. This is recurring, so Alpha will keep it as a small daily solution: read today's Ahmedabad forecast, write a warm short message, send it to your mom on WhatsApp each morning. Three pieces aren't connected yet: web access for the forecast, WhatsApp messaging, and daily scheduling. Messaging isn't planned for the first release, so automatic sending can't happen yet. What works today: you paste the forecast and Alpha writes the ready-to-send message for you to copy into WhatsApp. To finish the brief: what's your mom's number, what should the message include, and what send time?
